messages:
lina: Anyone seeing clients reconnect but the console still shows the old session as active for ~60s? We got duplicate stream events and a tiny billing blip :eye:

alex: yep, saw a small spike. Looks like resume TTL on the proxy isn't being expired when the edge drops. client reconnects -> new conn accepted, but session tombstone still considered alive by metrics.

marta: sample logs from a repro run: 
```
2026-03-22T15:04:01.123Z - conn=abc123 tenant=acme resume_token=rtk_42 state=active
2026-03-22T15:04:03.456Z - conn=def456 tenant=acme new_connect resume_token=rtk_42 -> accepted
2026-03-22T15:04:03.457Z - controller: duplicate_subscription detected tenant=acme token=rtk_42
2026-03-22T15:04:59.999Z - tombstone_cleanup: token=rtk_42 still referenced by proxy shard=shard-7
```

lina: The odd part — console shows 1 active session (the old one) and then the new one, so counts briefly go +1, but billing only charges one stream most of the time. Telemetry sampling attributes the spike to shard-2, not shard-7 where logs show the duplicate.

infra-bot: Deploy noticed: routing/proxy v2.14.1 rolled to canary at 2026-03-22T14:50:00Z; flag `resume_tombstone_grace_ms=60000` active in canary.

kevin: That flag was intended to avoid flapping for short disconnects, but if tombstone is tracked in two places (edge + controller) they can get out of sync. Console uses aggregated sampled counts and maps by route tag, while billing uses canonical controller events -> mismatch.

sam: Quick hypothesis: client reconnects to a different proxy instance before the original proxy cleaned up its in-memory lease; resume accepted, controller increments active sessions, sample router attributes to the original proxy's telemetry bucket (because of pre-aggregated sampling), console shows wrong shard attribution.

alex: Repro steps I used: 1) open ws to canary edge A, 2) force network drop, 3) reconnect to edge B within 500ms, 4) check /console/streams per-tenant. Happens reliably with resume_tombstone_grace_ms >= 30k.

marta: Potential fixes: 
- make resume acceptance require controller-confirmed tombstone release (adds RTT)
- keep tombstone owner sticky across proxy swap via consistent hashing for short window
- change console sampling to fall back to controller stream IDs rather than proxy tag when duplicates detected

kevin: Prefer changing console attribution and telemetry first (non-invasive). If console reads controller stream IDs when sampling collisions detected, we avoid misleading shard mappings. Then we can iterate on the sticky tombstone fix.

lina: +1 to non-invasive telemetry fix. Can someone scope: how often does this sampling fallback cost extra read ops?

sam: I can bench it. Rough estimate: worst-case extra controller reads ~0.5% of sampled events in our canary workload (because collisions are rare), trivial in cost.

infra-bot: Note: rolling back `resume_tombstone_grace_ms` to default 5s is an option, but will increase flapping if clients jitter.

alex: Action items: 
- sam to run a quick bench and post numbers (ETA 2h)
- marta to open telemetry PR for attribution fallback (ETA EOD)
- kevin to draft rollout note and flag changes for canary (ETA EOD)

marta: I'll include a small migration: console will prefer controller.stream_id when telemetry.sample_collision=true. Will include unit and integration tests.

lina: Thanks team. If bench shows low cost I'll push for the telemetry change today. For visibility: @product-obs FYI — small console attribution mismatch could show weird per-route spikes in dashboards.

kevin: also adding a short-term alert annotation in the console UI to highlight sample-attribution confidence (low/medium/high) so customers aren't chasing phantom shard spikes. :thumbsup:

sam: bench results: extra controller reads ~0.38% of sampled events; p95 latency increase for console refresh ~20ms. I'll paste logs in the PR.

marta: opened PR #4123 with tests and fallback. cc @kevin.

alex: LGTM on approach. Let's ship telemetry fallback to canary and monitor for attribution convergence.

lina: great, closing loop — when canary is green, we'll consider whether tombstone stickiness is worth the extra complexity. Thanks all :rocket:
